description_full: Aena S.M.E., S.A., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the management of airports in Spain, Brazil, the United Kingdom, Mexico, and Colombia. The company operates through Airports, Real Estate Services, Región de Murcia International Airport, and International segments. It also manages commercial spaces in airport terminals, and a network of car parks; and leasing or transfer use of land, office buildings, warehouses, hangars, and cargo vessels to airlines, air cargo operators, handling agents and other airport service providers. In addition, the company is involved in the operation of duty-free shops, food and beverage, and specialty shops; rental of cars; advertising; baggage wrapping machines; other vending machines; regulated services, including pharmacies, tobacconists, lottery vendors, etc.; and provision of financial services, such as currency exchange, VAT refunds, and ATMs, as well as advisory services to international airports. Aena S.M.E., S.A. was formerly known as Aena, S.A. and changed its name to Aena S.M.E., S.A. in April 2017. The company was founded in 1991 and is headquartered in Madrid, Spain. Aena S.M.E., S.A. operates as a subsidiary of Entidad Pública Empresarial ENAIRE.

financial_summary: Aena SME S.A. is a large-cap industrials business with a $47.7B market cap on $7.0B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +17% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +4.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 14% against a 8% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 67% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.9B in free cash flow — roughly 27 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.30× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 11.7×.

Shareholder yield of 3.5% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 52% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 4.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
